title: Defense Systems Acquisition Officer (I) (Maj to Capt) FMOS, MCSC
raw_text:
3. MOS 8816, Defense Systems Acquisition Officer (I) (Maj to Capt) FMOS,
MCSC

    a. Summary. Defense Systems Acquisition Officers have a graduate degree
in systems acquisition management and are members of the acquisition
workforce serving within an acquisition program office. They are responsible
for cost, schedule, and performance of critical acquisition projects or
programs within Marine Corps Systems Command or Naval Air Systems Command.

       b.   Prerequisites.   None.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Systems Acquisition Management Curriculum number 816
at the Naval Postgraduate School, Monterey, CA; or equivalent postgraduate
degree from an accredited university. Defense Systems Acquisition Officers
must have current knowledge of DOD, USN, and USMC Acquisition policy and
doctrine.

        (2) The officer must have earned a graduate degree in systems
acquisition management or a related field.

        (3) Subjects covered in the core courses should include acquisition
business analysis, program leadership and management theory, operations
analysis, fundamentals of cost benefit analysis, strategic acquisition
logistics, systems engineering for acquisition, acquisition program problem
solving, industry and government relationships, contract management and
administration, defense budget and financial management, acquisition testing




                                         1-343                       Enclosure (1)
 1147                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



and evaluation decision science and software acquisition management for
defense systems.

        (4) The officer must have completed a defense acquisition program
management capstone project and/or acquisition related thesis project.

        (5) Marines who have completed an equivalent postgraduate degree from
an accredited university and feel they meet the requirements for MOS 8816
should contact PM Competency Branch, Marine Corps Systems Command via
administrative action form for an evaluation and FMOS determination.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Perform the duties of an acquisition project officer within an
acquisition program office.

            (2) Responsible for cost/schedule/performance of assigned project(s).

        (3) Responsible for leading a cross-functional team engaged in
defense acquisition program activities.

        (4) Responsible for lifecycle management of assigned project(s) under
the guidance of a program manager.

        (5) Execute defense acquisition policies, strategies, plans and
procedures.

        (6) Apply advanced leadership, critical thinking, and operations
research techniques to defense acquisition problems.

        (7) Apply risk management and tradeoff decision analysis to defense
acquisition projects and programs.

        (8) Apply ethical considerations to defense acquisition, to include
procurement integrity, and defense acquisition standards of conduct.

        (9) Apply business and operating philosophies, concepts, practices,
and methodologies of defense industry with regard to systems acquisition,
particularly the application of sound business practices.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Management Analyst, 13-1111.

            (2) Project Management Specialist, 13-1082

            (3) Management, All Other, 11-9199

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
